steps.title: A Dão native
steps.body: Encruzado is a white grape native to the Dão, and grown almost nowhere else. It gives medium to full-bodied whites with citrus, white peach, pear, flowers and a mineral, sometimes smoky edge, with fresh acidity. It's often compared with white Burgundy for its texture and complexity.

steps.title: Making and ageing
steps.body: Encruzado takes well to barrel fermentation and lees ageing, which add creaminess and nutty notes without masking its fruit. It resists oxidation well. Good Encruzado ages 10 years or more, developing honey, nuts and toast. It's also blended with Malvasia Fina, Bical and Cerceal-Branco in Dão whites.

steps.prompt: Which white wine style is Encruzado often compared with?
steps.explanation: For its texture, complexity and response to oak.

steps.title: Why it matters
steps.body: Encruzado shows that Portugal, known for reds and Port, can make world-class whites. It needs careful handling in the vineyard, as it's prone to some diseases, and yields must be controlled. Producers like Quinta dos Roques and Quinta da Pellada helped establish its reputation.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Encruzado is the Dão's native white
Barrel fermentation and lees add texture
It can age 10 years or more
